ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: If mice are taken out of the web, what happens to the snake population?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: This is a forest food web diagram. In the lower left of the diagram there is a mouse labeled “Mouse”, in the lower right there is a snake labeled “Snake”, and there is an arrow pointing from the direction of the mouse toward the snake, indicating that food or energy flows from the mouse to the snake. Reasoning: In a food web, arrows usually indicate from the organism being eaten toward the predator, so the snake eats mice or depends on mice as a food source. If mice are removed from the food web, the food available to snakes decreases, therefore the snake population will decline.
